parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of gender expression or same-sex conduct; a comprehensive anti-discrimination statute (2010, expanded 2020) and hate-crime law covering gender identity (2013) plus a law against homophobic dissemination exist on paper. But enforcement is slow and uneven (one of nine complaints concluded by 2012; delayed reprimand), political hostility is active (2016 constitutional removal, 2021 school-campaign attacks), and social attitudes are disapproving (majorities against public expression, LGBT neighbours). Ten trans-targeted violence cases in 2023 cannot be benchmarked against a background rate in a small country — an open exposure. No visitor-specific border, facility, custody or care restrictions are documented, and none can be assumed. This sits in the reduced-risk band, below jurisdictions with documented working protections, above those with traveller-facing exposures.

entry_documents.protection: No border or document-screening restriction on trans visitors documented; LGR/document-marker practice unresolved, but the visitor uses home documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Marker-change position unresolved; foreign documents not reported as doubted.

investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented arrests, raids or custody practices targeting trans people; hate-crime law on the books.

federal_state_facilities.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers goods and services, including health care, from 2010; expanded 2020.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Enforcement of service protections uneven and slow.

care_services.exposure: A senior official publicly urged treating homosexuality as a disorder (2010) — dated; no current care denial to visitors documented.
care_services.protection: Health care covered by anti-discrimination law; mediated complaints show the mechanism operates.
care_services.interaction: Complaint resolution is slow; visitors may depart before outcomes.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Parliamentary hostility ('suspicious, revolting agenda'); 2016 constitutional removal of SO/GI protections under faith-leader pressure; social majorities disapprove of public LGBT expression.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2013 law criminalises dissemination of homophobic information; hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Enforcement of the dissemination law undocumented; hostility is political-climate, not state targeting of visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Anti-LGBT school campaigns by opposition lawmakers; education anti-bullying plan drew strong opposition — climate signal only; no minor-specific visitor exposure documented.
minors_guardians.protection: National action plan against bullying/discrimination in schools (2016) exists.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling families face no documented restriction; climate may be unwelcoming.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Ten trans-targeted violence cases logged by a community group in one year; no background-rate comparison possible — raw count, magnitude unknown.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute covers gender identity; UN expert visit (2024) signals state engagement; film-screening complaints mediated with one ruling in favour.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence not individually documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Complaint machinery is slow and bureaucratically impeded; trust lost among advocacy groups; hate-crime enforcement record beyond film complaints unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Anti-discrimination commissioner, ombudsman pledges, UN engagement provide functioning-institution climate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist on paper but resolve slowly; visitors rarely stay long enough to benefit.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor has a universal, state-imposed visitor-facing restriction (conduct register, routine refusal). This dossier documents no traveller-facing restriction at all — only uneven enforcement of protective law — so it sits far above 0.35.

0.55-B documents routine secondary screening and discretionary refusal of trans visitors. Here no border friction is documented, but social hostility and unremedied street violence are real; this case is somewhat above 0.55-B's exposure level.

0.75-D has equality law, occasional night-time violence, and remedies dependent on reporting. Very similar structure: protective statutes, uneven enforcement, documented street hostility. This dossier's slower complaint machinery and unbenchmarkable violence count place it at or just below 0.75-D.

0.95-A shows enforced equality law, respectful border practice, and quick remedies. This dossier's slow, distrusted complaint machinery and active political hostility keep it clearly below the 0.95 tier.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is law-protective but enforcement-lagging and socially disapproving. No criminal statute, no documented traveller-facing restriction at borders, in facilities, custody or care; the operative exposures are a ten-case annual log of trans-targeted violence that cannot be benchmarked, majoritarian disapproval of visible LGBT identity, and political threat-framing in schools and the constitution. Protections — anti-discrimination law, hate-crime coverage, anti-homophobia-dissemination law — are real but their remedies operate slowly, and the 2013 dissemination law's enforcement is unknown. This places the jurisdiction in the reduced-risk band, a step below the acceptance-with-working-protections tier and well above any tier-1 exposure.
